h: A Warm Start to a Swansea City Break
p: Plantasia is a brilliant shout for a first stop in Swansea, especially if you've arrived on a damp day. It's easy to spend a couple of hours inside, wandering among the tropical plants and hunting for animals hiding in the foliage. Talks and animal encounters are worth checking when you arrive, as they're often the highlight for curious kids. Then you can head back out into the city feeling warmed through.

Swansea has a lot to offer within walking distance. The National Waterfront Museum, in the Maritime Quarter, tells the story of industry and innovation in Wales, and it's free to visit. The Dylan Thomas Centre celebrates Swansea's most famous writer, born in the city in 1914, with exhibitions about his life and work. The Glynn Vivian Art Gallery, in the city centre, has a fine collection of art in an elegant building. Swansea Arena, which opened in 2022 alongside a new coastal park, brings big shows and concerts to the city.

Further along the bay, Mumbles is a charming seaside village with a pier, a lighthouse on the islands off the headland and a promenade lined with ice cream shops and cafés. Clyne Gardens, on the way there, is especially famous for its rhododendrons and azaleas in spring. Beyond Mumbles lies the Gower Peninsula, the first area in Britain to be named an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, with beaches such as Rhossili and Three Cliffs Bay among the most photographed in Wales. Put a warm morning at Plantasia with a breezy afternoon on the coast and you've got the best of both worlds.
